step1_analysis.circuit_type: CMOS Imager Pixel with Sigma-Delta ADC Front-End
step1_analysis.description: A pixel-parallel analog-to-digital conversion circuit featuring a differential comparator (op-amp) and an integrating feedback loop to form a first-order sigma-delta modulator.

paper_reference.title: A Low-Power Low-Noise Ultrawide-Dynamic-Range CMOS Imager with Pixel-Parallel A/D Conversion

power_consumption.description: Total DC power dissipation of the pixel circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: With the provided 0.9V bias, the tail current transistor (W/L=5/0.5) operates in strong inversion with Vov ~ 0.48V, yielding I_tail ~ 300uA. Total current is ~1mA, resulting in ~1.8mW power. The paper's 40nW requires subthreshold biasing (Vgs < 0.4V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated based on strong inversion square-law model for SKY130 at 0.9V bias.

gain_stage1.description: Low-frequency open-loop voltage gain of the differential pair (to node N0).

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm * Rout. In strong inversion, gm ~ 600uS, Rout ~ 30kOhm. Gain ~ 18 V/V = 25 dB. The 54 dB reported in the paper is achievable in subthreshold operation where intrinsic gain (gm*ro) is much higher.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for strong inversion operation due to the 0.9V bias in the testbench.

delay.description: Transient response delay of the comparator stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: Delay ~ C_load * dV / I_tail. With I_tail ~ 300uA and C_load ~ 50fF, slew rate is very high, leading to a delay of ~1-2 ns. The 100 ns reported corresponds to the much lower subthreshold currents.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Strong inversion currents charge parasitic capacitances much faster than the subthreshold currents used in the paper.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC open-loop gain of the comparator stages, and transient delay. Floating nodes N5 and N9 are biased to 0.9V to ensure convergence and balance the differential pair.
